newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Enough on OLOs' plate to go on diet in thin week.
newsitem.headline: Enough on OLOs' plate to go on diet in thin week.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) were slightly firmer on Monday, continuing Friday's advance on benign U.S. data, but volumes were slim and a pick-up in investor appetite was unlikely this week, dealers said.
Many blamed the closure of London markets today for the Spring bank holiday, an absence of major U.S. data this week and market holidays in Belgium on Thursday and Friday.

There was also concern about the outcome of French elections and France's post-election attitude to EMU as weekend opinion polls showed the anti-EMU Left gaining on the Right. The various factors meant OLOs would be range-bound this week, dealers said.
"The market will take a breather," said an analyst.

Some players were eyeing German production data due later today and forecast to show bond-positive slower growth DE-ECI. The figures combined with jobles numbers expected on Tuesday would leave OLOs stuck in a range versus Bunds, he added.
The 10-year OLO/Bund spread widened to 11 basis points at 0835 GMT from 10 on Friday as some of the pressure on French OATs from the election worries wafted over to the Belgian market MEUR.
But dealers said there was no reason to expect the current 5-15 bp range would be cracked.
Noting the benchmark OLO had gained over a full point over the past week, one analyst said the bond was looking overbought. "A downward correction in the coming days cannot be excluded," he said.
